**Repaired finding submitted: compliant (AUDIT).**

What changed and why:

- **Withdrew the deviation and the redline.** The verifier is right on scope: § 11.3 is an AUP/content-warranty enforcement right (investigate suspected unlawful or abusive Content, then remove/restrict/terminate), not verification of our usage or charges. The AUDIT rule's parameters — independent auditor, frequency cap, underpayment true-up at 5%/10% — presuppose a usage/fee audit and produced incoherent language when imported (a § 11.2(b) content investigation cannot yield an "underpayment"), an unworkable once-a-year cap on abuse investigations, and an absolute 15-day notice condition that overrode the existing emergency/required-by-law carve-out in p0137.
- **Classified as compliant.** No usage, licence or fee-compliance audit right binding Customer exists anywhere in the Agreement (no hits for audit/inspect/verify/records/monitor; §§ 11.5 and 13.2 add nothing). That absence is better than the preferred position and favourable to us, so it is not raised as a deviation or as missing.
- **Noted, not flagged:** § 11.3 lacks confidentiality obligations on investigators and any express limit on access to Customer systems, and its notice is best-efforts and attached only to restriction/removal. If § 11.3 is reopened for other reasons, the narrow asks (notice where practicable, investigator confidentiality, no access to our systems beyond what is necessary) can be raised then; suspension/termination remedies belong to those rules.
